LESSON: DATA REPRESENTATION AND INTERPRETATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Data Handling and Probability
Topic 5.1: Data Representation and Interpretation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Data Representation and Interpretation, part of Data Handling and Probability in Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: where possible learners use the hand 1. What are the different ways of representing data? 2. How do we determine the mean of data?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collect data from their own experiences, for example size of shoes, height or test scores,

3. discuss and interpret bar graphs,

4. discuss and represent data in line graphs,

5. discuss and interpret line graphs,

6. recognise the mode from a given set of discrete data,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Data Representation and Interpretation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses and represents data in line graphs.

• Critical thinking and Problem solving: as the learner discusses and interprets bar graphs.

• Self-efficacy: as the learner collects data from their own experiences, for example size of shoes, height or test scores.
